I’ve long felt that a $SPCX - $TSLA deal is inevitable since Elon controls 48% of $SPCX as-converted shares and 10.5% of TSLA shares. Since any deal would be $SPCX stock for $TSLA stock the deal will not be as compelling as many on X believe, given the massive dilution and all-equity economics.  I expect a SPCX offer price in the neighborhood of $420/TSLA share, and as in most stock-for-stock deals will likely get arbitraged down given the approximate 6-12 months needed between a deal announcement and deal close.  

I would expect the combined SPCX/TSLA multiple of EBITDA or EPS to follow the acquiring company’s multiple, which in this case is $SPCX and is lower than TSLA’s FY’27 EV/Ebitda multiple (TSLA 72.6x, SPCX 29.4x).  All told, I don’t expect a huge windfall for TSLA shareholders on a SPCX/TSLA stock-for-stock deal, although the announcement itself would be positive for TSLA stock.

text:
US inflation remains too high.

And I expect it to stay that way.

But underlying inflation looks less alarming. According to the Atlanta Fed, sticky-price inflation, which measures prices that change relatively infrequently, runs well below headline inflation: 2.8% versus 3.7%.

In late 2022, "sticky" prices were rising at a 6.7% annual rate.

With financial conditions already tightening since August, this could give the Federal Reserve a way out of several additional rate hikes.

An October rate hike is not really on the table, but it will be interesting to see whether Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who rarely gives much away at FOMC press conferences, acknowledges any of this.

I believe inflation around 3% will become the new normal.

And if headline inflation falls from today's 3.7% to, say, 2.8%, matching sticky-price inflation, I expect both investors and the Fed to celebrate.

Not because inflation has been defeated. But because it would give the Fed a chance to halt its rate-hiking cycle.

At that point, the Fed may be ready to declare victory at 3% inflation and leave markets alone. But your purchasing power won't be celebrating just yet.

zh_summary: 프리컴파일과 EVM은 이더리움에 대부분의 암호화 지원을 넣는 잘못된 위치다. 왜냐하면 그것들은 체인에 calldata로 포함되어야 하는 데이터에서 작동하며, PeerDAS가 있어도 약 8 MB/s의 실질적 한계가 있다. 이더리움은 암호화 세계 컴퓨터이므로 메인 실행 스레드에 필요하지 않은 데이터/계산은 그기에 두지 않아야 한다. 더 넓은 암호화 지원의 이상적 경로는 다른 메커니즘을 통하는 것이다.
text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.
